### 2026-10-11 — Do not edit sentences in a dated document; add a status block and a history banner

*Plain summary: three review rounds on the stale egress wording kept finding new false statements because I rewrote sentence by sentence; the fourth attempt adds one dated "Status as of 2026-10-11" block per document, marks the old body as dated history, and leaves what was true on its date alone.*

The ADR-027 header (Architecture Decision Record 027) said NOT YET ACTIVE, the two egress guides said built and dormant with an empty allowlist, and the data map said the air-gap stays welded, while web search to Kagi has been live since 2026-07-02. My first pass (f2639a23), second (c5849c37) and third (09b5bd69), which exist only on the unmerged branch docs/1749-stale-posture, each rewrote the old sentences to be "less wrong", and each review found fresh errors in the rewrite: the first sanctioned external fetch was 2026-06-12 (a smoke-harness run under Amendment 1's preconditions with the Lead Architect present), not the 2026-07-02 ceremony, which was the first standing allowlist entry; the socket-level allowlist is per fetch and empty at rest, while the standing list is a different object; and `[guest_parser] enabled = false` closes nothing, because a normal launcher boot never reaches the code that reads it and a `--go-live` boot overrides it. One round also rewrote true dated history into a false present-tense claim. The pattern was that every edited sentence is a new claim that has to be re-verified, and a sentence about a past date has no business being edited at all.

This pass re-read each fact in code before writing it: the single call site of `_maybe_start_guest_parser` inside `if _go_live_requested():`, the on-only environment override in `launcher/guest_parser.py`, the Assistant Orchestrator (AO) and launcher registration sites for the request-keyed adjudicator, the door's step 1 (not HTTPS (encrypted web traffic), userinfo, raw IP address, bad port) and step 2.5 (names resolving to internal ranges) refusals, `guarded_fetch.py` as the only non-test caller of `allow_external_endpoint`, the checker class (578 to 866) and its `check` method (712 to 866), and that importing the module loads openvino, openvino_genai, numpy and pydantic (observed in `sys.modules`, no network). Then each document got a banner marking its body as dated history and one status block, and the runbook and register sentences that stated a lock as a present-tense fact had only the false clause replaced. Trade-off: the pages now carry two eras at once and are longer, but a reader can tell which era a sentence belongs to, and nobody has to trust that I re-derived 285 lines of ADR correctly. Branch docs/1749-posture-v2 off main; the old branch docs/1749-stale-posture is left untouched.

**Next:** the levers that do not control the paste door (the `[guest_parser]` flag, the empty-allowlist and registration locks, the "refused by rule" line in `permission_profile.py`, the stale docstrings in `url_adjudicator.py` and `guarded_fetch.py`) are design work under #1751, as are these stale code statements: the `entrypoint.py` registration docstring (~7480, "RULE 3 + the EMPTY allowlist deny every URL at the door"), the `_arm_egress_guard` docstring in `launcher/__main__.py` ("STAGED/DORMANT... allowlist empty"), the `launcher/config/default.toml` comment that `false` means the launcher never touches the VM (dead in both boot modes), the `url_adjudicator.py` docstring listing GET-only while the door accepts POST under the paste purpose, and the dated flag statements in `docs/security/guest_parser_provisioning_record.md` section 5 and ADR-034 (~122); this documentation fix is #1749.
